# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles 198 coordinate-anchored settlement trajectories and 228 excluded ledger candidates across the Pacific Northwest (USGS Hydrological Unit 17, 712.506 km²) from 10000BC to 1600AD. Spanning 426 ledger candidates across Washington (79), Idaho (65), Oregon (47) and northern Nevada (7), the inventory captures terminal Pleistocene occupations at Cooper's Ferry (10000BC to 130 in 500AD), Paisley Caves (10000BC to 50 in 4000BC), Manis Mastodon (10000BC to 30 in 8000BC) and East Wenatchee (Richey-Roberts) (10000BC to 25 in 9000BC) [@jenkins2012paisley; @waters2011manis], deep-time canyon continuity at Five Mile Rapids-Celilo (8500BC to 1.600 in 1600AD), Celilo Falls (Wyam) (5000BC to 850 in 1600AD), Kettle Falls (6500BC to 560 in 1600AD) and Windust Caves (8500BC to 110 in 500AD) [@cressman1960dalles], Coast Salish and Makah coastal towns at Everett Port Gardner Metropolis (1.780), Tacoma Commencement Capital (1.550), Bellingham Whatcom Capital (1.420), Ozette (1.150), Tse-whit-zen (1.120) and Old Man House (920) [@matson1995northwest; @samuels1991ozette; @rorabaugh2023salish], Lower Columbia Chinookan and Kalapuya centres at Oregon City Falls Capital (1.820), Portland Willamette Capital (1.720), Cathlapotle (1.200), Meier-Multnomah (950), Kalapuya-Champoeg (780) and Multnomah (Sauvie Island) (610) [@sobel2006cathlapotle; @ames1992meier], and Interior Plateau or Snake River centres led by Lapwai Council Capital (1.780), Lewiston Clearwater Capital (1.620), Clarkston Snake Metropolis (1.210) and American Falls Cataract Capital (1.180).

# Background

Sedentary settlement in HU 17 developed around predictable marine, estuarine and river-canyon bottlenecks rather than cereal agriculture [@ames1999northwest; @matson1995northwest]. Deeply stratified shellmiddens, wet-site cedar plank-house villages preserved by mudslides (Ozette) and multi-millennial canyon fishery terraces provide continuous demographic sequences across all four watershed sub-regions [@samuels1991ozette; @sobel2006cathlapotle].

At the Pleistocene-Holocene root, early cave and terrace occupations at Paisley Caves (10000BC to 4000BC, peaking at 50), Manis Mastodon (10000BC to 8000BC, peaking at 30), East Wenatchee (Richey-Roberts) (10000BC to 9000BC, peaking at 25) and Cooper's Ferry (10000BC to 500AD, peaking at 130) anchor initial sparse foraging populations inside the gazetteer [@jenkins2012paisley; @waters2011manis], while 205 duplicate heritage pins within 2 km and 23 unquantified non-habitation cave or rockshelter records (such as Marmes Rockshelter, Rimrock Draw Rockshelter, Wilson Butte Cave, Fort Rock Cave, Owl Cave (Wasden) and Jaguar Cave) are excluded in the source ledger to prevent double counting [@fryxell1968marmes].

# Methodology

## Inclusion Rules and Plank-House Demographic Estimation

All 426 candidate records in the regional source ledger follow Operation Viscount screening rules. Consolidating 205 duplicate coordinate or alias records within 2 km and filtering 23 unquantified non-habitation cave or rockshelter records leaves 198 permanent settlements across four sub-regions (42 in Puget Sound-Olympic Coast, 25 in Lower Columbia-Willamette, 46 in Columbia Plateau-Dalles and 85 in Snake River-High Desert).

Population series apply coastal and riverine hearth-and-plank-house multipliers: 25 to 45 inhabitants per multi-family Chinookan or Coast Salish cedar plank-house [@ames1992meier; @sobel2006cathlapotle; @samuels1991ozette], ethnohistoric village-count anchors along the Lower Columbia and Willamette [@boyd1999northwest], pithouse depression counts on the Columbia Plateau [@cressman1960dalles], and high-desert wetland or canyon winter-village counts across the Snake River Plain and Owyhee basin.

# Testing and Validation

Gazetteer auditing passed all reconciliation checks at 0 errors at GMT+0:

1. **Ledger Parity**: All 426 ledger entries (198 included, 228 excluded) reconcile cleanly against the settlement trajectories (732 point-observations, mean 3,7 observations per settlement, 187 settlements with at least 3 horizons, cumulative peak sum 107.675).
2. **Coordinate Compliance**: All 198 records carry valid coordinates (41,19 N to 48,86 N, 111,45 W to 124,71 W) and strictly positive integer trajectories across four states (79 Washington, 65 Idaho, 47 Oregon and 7 Nevada).
3. **Sub-Regional Mass Conservation**: Explicit settlement totals represent 12,53% of total HU 17 population in 1500AD (24.060 of 192k) and 16,95% in 1600AD (35.520 of 209,5k), leaving positive rural residuals across all four sub-regions.

```{r tbl-gazetteer, results='asis'}
fmt_coord <- function(cvec) {
  lat <- as.numeric(cvec[[1]])
  lon <- as.numeric(cvec[[2]])
  paste0(viscount_fmt_number(abs(lat), 2L), " N, ", viscount_fmt_number(abs(lon), 2L), " W")
}

reg_short <- list(
  nw_puget_sound_olympic_coast = "Puget-Olympic",
  nw_lower_columbia_willamette_coast = "Lower Columbia",
  nw_columbia_plateau_yakima_spokane = "Columbia Plateau",
  nw_snake_river_klamath_interior = "Snake-High Desert"
)

clean_text <- function(txt) {
  txt <- as.character(txt)
  txt <- gsub("CENTAUR Existing Verified Monument Inventory", "CENTAUR Monument Inventory", txt, fixed = TRUE)
  txt <- gsub("Existing Verified ", "", txt, fixed = TRUE)
  txt <- gsub("coordinate/alias", "coordinate or alias", txt, fixed = TRUE)
  txt <- gsub(" (cave/rockshelter/mine/quarry/medicine wheel/cemetery/kill site)", "", txt, fixed = TRUE)
  txt <- gsub("/", " and ", txt, fixed = TRUE)
  txt <- gsub(" & ", " and ", txt, fixed = TRUE)
  txt <- gsub("&", " and ", txt, fixed = TRUE)
  txt <- gsub("_", " ", txt, fixed = TRUE)
  txt <- gsub("#", "", txt, fixed = TRUE)
  txt <- gsub("%", " per cent", txt, fixed = TRUE)
  txt
}

rows <- lapply(names(sett), function(sk) {
  sv <- sett[[sk]]
  p_vec <- unlist(sv$population)
  yrs <- as.integer(names(p_vec))
  p_vals <- as.numeric(p_vec)
  pk_idx <- which.max(p_vals)
  min_yr_str <- ifelse(min(yrs) < 0, paste0(abs(min(yrs)), "BC"), paste0(min(yrs), "AD"))
  max_yr_str <- ifelse(max(yrs) < 0, paste0(abs(max(yrs)), "BC"), paste0(max(yrs), "AD"))
  span_str <- if (min(yrs) == max(yrs)) min_yr_str else paste0(min_yr_str, " to ", max_yr_str)
  pk_yr_str <- ifelse(yrs[pk_idx] < 0, paste0(abs(yrs[pk_idx]), "BC"), paste0(yrs[pk_idx], "AD"))
  data.frame(
    Settlement = clean_text(sv$name),
    Polity = clean_text(sv$country),
    SubRegion = reg_short[[sv$region_id]],
    Coords = fmt_coord(sv$coords),
    Span = span_str,
    PeakYear = pk_yr_str,
    PeakPop = viscount_fmt_number(p_vals[pk_idx], 0L),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    pk_num = p_vals[pk_idx]
  )
})
df_gaz <- do.call(rbind, rows)
df_gaz <- df_gaz[order(-df_gaz$pk_num, df_gaz$Settlement), ]
df_gaz <- head(df_gaz, 45L)
df_gaz$pk_num <- NULL
rownames(df_gaz) <- NULL

viscount_table(
  df_gaz,
  "Top 45 settlements by peak population across the 198 catalogued sites in the Northwest (HU 17) gazetteer.",
  c("Settlement", "Jurisdiction", "Sub-Region", "Coordinates", "Span", "Peak Year", "Peak Pop.")
)
```

# Results

## Puget Sound and Lower Columbia Plank-House Towns

Coastal and estuarine towns dominated the upper rank-size tier of HU 17 (Table 1 and Figure 1). Across Puget Sound and the Strait of Juan de Fuca (42 sites), Everett Port Gardner Metropolis (48 N, 122,2 W) peaked at 1.780 in 1600AD, Tacoma Commencement Capital (47,25 N, 122,45 W) reached 1.550 in 1600AD, Bellingham Whatcom Capital (48,75 N, 122,48 W) reached 1.420 in 1300AD, Tumwater Deschutes Falls Capital reached 1.390 in 1250AD, Marysville Tulalip Capital reached 1.310 in 1300AD, Mukilteo Point Elliott Capital reached 1.240 in 1300AD, Ozette (48,21 N, 124,71 W) rose to 1.150 in 1600AD, Tse-whit-zen (48,12 N, 123,45 W) grew from 1000BC to 1.120 in 1600AD and Old Man House (47,72 N, 122,55 W) expanded from 500AD to 920 in 1600AD, joined by Anacortes Fidalgo Capital (1.090), Auburn Green River Capital (1.080), Duwamish Head (420) and Lummi (Point Francis) (420) [@samuels1991ozette; @rorabaugh2023salish].

Along the Lower Columbia-Wapato Valley and Oregon-Washington outer coast (25 sites), Oregon City Falls Capital (45,35 N, 122,6 W) peaked at 1.820 in 1550AD, Portland Willamette Capital (45,52 N, 122,68 W) reached 1.720 in 1600AD, Cathlapotle (45,85 N, 122,76 W) rose from 1400AD to 1.200 in 1600AD, Meier-Multnomah grew from 1400AD to 950 in 1600AD, Kalapuya-Champoeg reached 780 in 1600AD, Multnomah (Sauvie Island) reached 610, Neah Bay (48,37 N, 124,62 W) reached 520, Cascades (Watlala) reached 490, Willapa Bay (Chinook Point) reached 480 and Clatsop reached 460 [@sobel2006cathlapotle; @ames1992meier; @boyd1999northwest].

## Columbia Plateau Fisheries and Snake River Interior

On the Columbia Plateau (46 sites), Five Mile Rapids-Celilo (45,64 N, 121,12 W) exhibits one of the deepest continuous sequences in HU 17, spanning 8500BC to 1.600 in 1600AD as the premier Plateau salmon-trading nexus [@cressman1960dalles]. It is joined by Walla Walla Mill Creek Capital (46,07 N, 118,33 W, 1.090 in 1350AD), Celilo Falls (Wyam) (5000BC to 850 in 1600AD), Rufus John Day Rapids Town (810 in 1400AD), Kettle Falls (6500BC to 560 in 1600AD), Priest Rapids (460), Walla Walla (Wallula) (460), Miller Site (Miller Island) (450) and Windust Caves (8500BC to 110 in 500AD). Across the Snake River Plain and Harney-Owyhee high desert (85 sites), major interior capitals include Lapwai Council Capital (46,4 N, 116,8 W, 1.780 in 1550AD), Lewiston Clearwater Capital (46,42 N, 117,02 W, 1.620 in 1550AD), Clarkston Snake Metropolis (46,42 N, 117,05 W, 1.210 in 1300AD), American Falls Cataract Capital (42,78 N, 112,85 W, 1.180 in 1350AD), Idaho Falls Cataract Capital (1.120 in 1350AD), St. Anthony Henrys Fork Capital (820 in 1350AD) and Almo City of Rocks Town (810 in 1350AD, marking the rank-45 threshold in Table 1), alongside Hagerman-Bliss (450), Nampa (Deer Flat) (240), American Falls (240), Weiser (Mann Creek) (230) and Bruneau (Bliss) (220).

```{r tbl-ledger, results='asis'}
cand <- ledger$candidates
exc <- cand[cand$status == "excluded", , drop = FALSE]
exc <- rbind(exc[exc$reason != "duplicate_alias", , drop = FALSE], exc[exc$reason == "duplicate_alias", , drop = FALSE])
if (nrow(exc) > 30L) exc <- exc[seq_len(30L), , drop = FALSE]
df_led <- data.frame(
  Candidate = clean_text(exc$name),
  StateCountry = clean_text(exc$country),
  Status = clean_text(exc$status),
  Reason = clean_text(exc$reason),
  Details = clean_text(exc$justification),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
rownames(df_led) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_led,
  "Representative 30 of 228 excluded candidates (426 total) in the Northwest (HU 17) source ledger.",
  c("Candidate Site", "Jurisdiction", "Status", "Exclusion Reason", "Consolidation Note")
)
```

# Limitations

Plateau and coastal populations underwent strong seasonal mobility between winter plank-house or pithouse villages and summer fishing or root-gathering camps such as Celilo Falls [@cressman1960dalles; @ames1999northwest]. Annualised integer benchmarks smooth these intra-year swings, and hundreds of smaller Chinookan, Salish, Sahaptin and Northern Paiute camps remain absorbed within the continuous kriged rural surface [@kelly2025].
